title: Recall Response
description:
What memory_recall returns.

Two consumers, one response. `records` is for a host that wants to reason over structure. `context_block` is for a host that just wants text to paste into a prompt — pre-formatted, token-bounded, and never exceeding the caller's max_tokens. The second is what makes this safe to call inside a loop: memory can never quietly eat the host's context window.

records.description: Ranked results, best first. Each entry wraps the record with the score that got it there, so a host can tune retrieval without guessing.

context_block.description: Ready-to-inject text rendering of the records that fit the budget. Records marked sensitivity='pii' or 'secret' are excluded unless the caller explicitly opted in. Empty string when nothing was recalled — never a placeholder sentence, which a model would otherwise treat as a fact.

token_count.description: Actual token count of context_block, measured not estimated. Guaranteed <= the caller's max_tokens.

truncated.description: True when the token budget cut off records that otherwise qualified.

omitted_count.description: How many qualifying records did not fit. A host seeing a large number here should either raise max_tokens or narrow its query — not assume it saw everything.

excluded_sensitive_count.description: How many records were withheld from context_block on sensitivity grounds. Reported so redaction is visible rather than silent.

contradictions.description: Pairs among the returned records that are in tension. Surfaced rather than resolved: the memory agent will not pick a winner on the host's behalf.

query_echo.description: The effective query after defaults and policy were applied. Echoed back because a host that gets surprising results needs to see what was actually run, not what it thinks it asked.

degraded.description: Set when recall ran without full capability — e.g. the vector extension failed to load and the query fell back to keyword-only. The result is still usable, but a host must not read a thin result as 'nothing is known'.

record.description: The full record, matching whichever of the three record schemas its type indicates.

in_context_block.description: Whether this record made it into context_block, or was returned as structure only.

score_breakdown.description: Every term that produced the total, so retrieval is tunable rather than a black box.

relevance.description: Fused relevance: reciprocal-rank fusion of the vector and keyword rankings.

recency.description: exp(-lambda * hours_since_last_access), lambda derived from the configured half-life.

vector_similarity.description: Raw cosine similarity, or null when the vector path was unavailable or the strategy was keyword-only.

keyword_rank.description: BM25 rank from FTS5, or null when the record was matched only by vector.
